    Dim rs As Object
    Dim li As Object

    Set rs = CreateObject("ADODB.Recordset")

        Set li = ListView1.ListItems.Add(, , rs!Name)

        rs.MoveNext
    Loop

    cn.Close

In your case the text is "ten", which isn't numeric at all, so `Val` would return 0 — but at least it wouldn't crash.

title: "how do I make an MDI app"

steps.prompt: How do I make an MDI app?

answers.text:
To make an MDI app in VibeBasic:

1. Create an **MDIForm** — this is the parent window. It can only contain Align controls and invisible controls (no regular buttons or text boxes directly on it).
2. Create your child forms and set their **MDIChild = True** property. When you call `f.Show`, the form appears inside the MDIForm.
3. In the MDIForm, you can use **AutoShowChildren** (True to auto-show new children), **ScrollBars**, and the **Arrange** method (`MDIForm1.Arrange vbCascade`, `vbTileHorizontal`, or `vbTileVertical`).
4. **MDIForm1.ActiveForm** gives you the currently active child form.
5. If you have a menu, set **WindowList = True** on a menu item to get an automatic list of open child windows.
6. To open a new instance of a child form from code: `Set f = New Form2: f.Show`.

That's the full picture — the MDIForm is the shell, child forms with MDIChild = True live inside it, and the WindowList menu item and Arrange method handle window management.

    Dim words() As String

    Next k

title: "how do I make an MDI app"

steps.prompt: How do I make an MDI app?

answers.text:
To make an MDI app in VibeBasic:

1. Create an **MDIForm** (e.g. `MDIForm1`) — this is the parent window. It can only contain Align controls and invisible controls (no regular buttons or labels directly on it).
2. For each child form, set its **MDIChild = True** property.
3. Open a child with `Form2.Show` (or `Set f = New Form2: f.Show` for multiple instances). The child appears inside the MDIForm automatically.
4. Use `MDIForm1.Arrange vbCascade` (or `vbTileHorizontal`, `vbTileVertical`) to arrange the open children.
5. `MDIForm1.ActiveForm` gives you the currently active child form.
6. If you add a menu item with **WindowList = True**, it will automatically list all open child windows.
7. The MDIForm has its own `MDIForm_Load` event (not `Form_Load`) for initialization.
8. The MDIForm also has `AutoShowChildren` (auto-show/hide children when the parent is shown/hidden) and `ScrollBars` for when children overflow.

That's the whole pattern: one MDIForm as the shell, child forms with `MDIChild = True`, and you manage them from the MDIForm's code.

title: "how do I make an MDI app"

steps.prompt: How do I make an MDI app?

answers.text: To make an MDI app in VibeBasic, you need an **MDIForm** (the parent window) and one or more regular forms with **MDIChild = True** (the child windows). The MDIForm can only contain Align controls and invisible controls; all visible content goes on the child forms. In the MDIForm's Load event, you typically create and show the first child: `Set f = New Form2: f.Show`. Each child form appears inside the MDIForm's client area. You can access the currently active child with `MDIForm1.ActiveForm`, and arrange all children with `MDIForm1.Arrange vbCascade` (or `vbTileHorizontal` / `vbTileVertical`). If you add a menu item with **WindowList = True**, it will automatically list all open child windows so the user can switch between them. The MDIForm also has **AutoShowChildren** (show/hide children when the parent is shown/hidden) and **ScrollBars** for when children overflow. To open additional instances of a child at runtime, just repeat `Set f = New Form2: f.Show`.
